daily_guide.reference: Georgia DNR-linked guide, Game Species Daily Limits, updated August 27, 2026

general_guide.reference: Georgia DNR-linked guide, General Regulations, updated August 27, 2026

season_rules.reference: Rule 391-4-3-.03(5): continuous freshwater baseline season, subject to other laws and local exceptions

size_rules.reference: Rule 391-4-3-.06(1)(a)(8), (1)(d), and (2): baseline length minima and other size limits

sturgeon_guide.reference: Georgia DNR-linked guide, Game Species Daily Limits, updated August 27, 2026: sturgeon may not be taken in Georgia

warnings: Statewide baseline only. Waterbody and border-water overrides are not evaluated.
Daily and combined possession limits are displayed, not checked against retained fish.
Seasons, licenses, fishing methods, closures and protected-species restrictions are not evaluated.
Length results do not establish whether a fish may be kept. Confirm species and consult current official rules.

black_bass.guidance: Combined black bass limit; a five-fish sublimit covers smallmouth and other specified bass.

temperate_bass.guidance: Combined white, striped and hybrid bass limit; at most two may measure 22 inches or more.

bream.guidance: Combined eligible sunfish/bream limit, not a separate allowance per species.

crappie.guidance: Black and white crappie share this limit.

trout.guidance: Combined mountain trout limit, including brook, rainbow and brown trout.

pickerel.guidance: Combined chain, grass and redfin pickerel limit.

channel_flathead_catfish.guidance: The daily-limit guide lists no statewide limit for channel and flathead catfish; local limits still apply.

exception_notes: Some lakes have higher minima, no minimum, or a protected slot; statewide comparison does not resolve those waters.
Smallmouth contributes to the combined five-fish bass sublimit; shared waters can differ.
Lake Lanier imposes a local length minimum.
River sections and border waters impose different length and count limits; striped bass also has seasonal restrictions.
Public fishing areas and shared waters can have different limits.
Check shared-water rules and posted restrictions.
Waters Creek and Noontootla Creek have length restrictions; special trout waters can require release or impose other limits.
Length guidance has not been reviewed for this demo. Public fishing areas can limit channel catfish.
No species-specific baseline has been reviewed. Do not infer unrestricted harvest, including for protected species or unresolved taxa.

notes: Season describes calendar availability for ordinary recreational fishing, not overall harvest permission.
Local and border-water exceptions, method-specific seasons, daily limits and stocking schedules are excluded.
No verified restriction means the parameter was reviewed without finding a statewide size boundary; it is not a harvest authorization.
Not reviewed means applicability is unresolved, not that the parameter is unrestricted.
Species parameters are descriptive data only and are not consumed by the current regulation checker.
